title.narrative: HARPS "Humanitarian Assistance for Resilience in Protection and Shelter, Ensuring Nutrition and Safety in contested area 3."

description.narrative: ltpgtHARPS is a multifaceted initiative designed to provide critical support to displaced and conflict-affected populations, including internally displaced persons, returnees, and vulnerable host communities. These populations face compounded challenges such as inadequate housing, malnutrition, and heightened protection risks due to prolonged displacement and conflict. The project seeks to address these needs through targeted interventions that enhance living conditions, promote safety, and foster resilience. Its main objectives include providing emergency shelter, improving nutrition for at-risk individuals, and strengthening protection mechanisms, ensuring the inclusion of marginalized groups such as persons with disabilities, women, and older adults.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe project targets Contested Area 3, where the needs for shelter, nutrition, and protection are most critical, using a community-driven approach to involve local stakeholders at every stage of implementation. Key activities include providing rental assistance through formal tenancy agreements, distributing repair kits, and enhancing maternal and child health services. Protection initiatives focus on offering psychosocial support, strengthening community-based child protection systems, and providing multi-purpose cash assistance for vulnerable children to meet basic needs, access education, secure legal protection, and prevent exploitation and violence. Accountability is ensured through mechanisms like structured feedback systems.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtAdditionally, the project addresses the humanitarian response needs of returnees and IDPs, many of whom lack formal land ownership documentation, hindering their ability to claim or defend their rights. To address this, the project emphasizes community-based and legal frameworks to resolve disputes, housing, land, and property (HLP) counseling, and HLP training. While the project’s focus is limited to these three sectors, it actively collaborates with local actors to enhance outcomes and maximize its impact.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtDeliverables include secure housing arrangements, reduced malnutrition rates, and strengthened community-based protection systems, achieved over a 12-month period with milestones such as beneficiary selection, resource distribution, and post-distribution monitoring. The budget allocation, set at 50% for shelter, 30% for nutrition, and 20% for protection, ensures strategic use of available resources, supported by trained teams and robust partnerships. Stakeholders, including humanitarian agencies, local governments, and community leaders, play a vital role in ensuring fair and inclusive implementation.lt/pgtltpgtExpected outcomes include improved stability through safe shelter, better health through nutrition interventions, and enhanced resilience and security via strengthened protection measures. The initiative accounts for risks such as limited resources, security challenges, and potential disputes, deploying mitigation strategies such as community engagement, flexible implementation, and conflict-sensitive planning. This project represents a vital opportunity to not only address immediate needs but also build a foundation for sustainable recovery and empowerment, creating a path toward hope and dignity for affected populations.ltbrgtlt/pgt
